overlapping_phenotypes: Progressive childhood dystonia, gait impairment, parkinsonian signs
discriminating_phenotype: Anterior commissure agenesis and corpus callosum dysgenesis without T2*/SWI brain iron accumulation
discriminating_logic: Classical NBIA demonstrates iron accumulation on T2*/SWI (e.g., eye-of-the-tiger sign in PKAN) and lacks anterior commissure agenesis. Instead, anterior commissure and corpus callosum dysgenesis without pathological iron deposition distinguish ACBD6.

overlapping_phenotypes: Severe early-onset developmental delay, hypotonia, prominent hyperkinetic movement disorder (dystonia and chorea)
discriminating_phenotype: Insidious chronic progressive dystonia with early postural deformities, ataxia, and structural commissural dysgenesis
discriminating_logic: GNAO1 is typically driven by acute, life-threatening hyperkinetic choreic or dystonic crises (status dystonicus), whereas ACBD6 exhibits a more insidious, chronic progressive dystonia (94%) with early postural deformities (97%), ataxia (85%), and structural commissural dysgenesis.

discriminating_phenotype: Dominant progressive dystonia and commissural agenesis without brain-lung-thyroid triad
discriminating_logic: NKX2-1 typically presents with the 'brain-lung-thyroid' triad (congenital hypothyroidism, respiratory distress syndrome, chorea) without profound intellectual disability or commissural agenesis. Dystonia is the dominant feature in ACBD6 (94%), while classic chorea is far less prominent.

discriminating_phenotype: Focal brainstem anomalies (short midbrain and small inferior vermis) without generalized pontocerebellar devastation
discriminating_logic: PCH presents with severe, diffuse pontine and generalized cerebellar hemispheric atrophy. In contrast, ACBD6 brainstem anomalies are strictly focal (short midbrain in 38% and small inferior vermis in 38%) without generalized pontocerebellar devastation.
